reason: Ruby's `include` is a receiver method on the class; trails' `include()` (activesupport/src/include.ts) is a free function, so the class it mixes into is its first argument. The settled trails idiom for `include` (CLAUDE.md § "Module mixins").
`BCrypt::Password.new(digest)` (secure_password.rb:210,217) is one-shot `bcrypt.compareSync` / `bcrypt.getSalt` in node, which exposes no Password object to construct. Language shortcoming.
